events.text: Jan van Eyck completes and signs the oil painting, dated 1434.

evidence.quote: is a 1434 oil painting on oak panel by the Early Netherlandish painter Jan van Eyck .
Signed and dated by van Eyck in 1434

events.text: Don Diego de Guevara gives the portrait to Margaret of Austria.

evidence.quote: By 1516 he had given the portrait to Margaret of Austria

events.text: Painting inherited by Margaret's niece Mary of Hungary.

evidence.quote: In 1530 the painting was inherited by Margarets niece Mary of Hungary

events.text: Painting inherited by Philip II of Spain after Mary's death.

evidence.quote: inventory taken after her death in 1558 , when it was inherited by Philip II of Spain

events.text: German visitor sees the painting in the Alcazar Palace, Madrid.

evidence.quote: In 1599 a German visitor saw it in the Alcazar Palace in Madrid

events.text: Painting moved to the Palacio Nuevo, Madrid, after the Alcazar fire.

evidence.quote: by 1794 had been moved to the Palacio Nuevo

events.text: Painting in London, in the possession of Colonel James Hay.

evidence.quote: In 1816 the painting was in London , in the possession of Colonel James Hay

events.text: Prince Regent returns the painting to Hay after two years on approval.
Hay gives the painting to a friend to look after.

evidence.quote: Around 1828 , Hay gave it to a friend to look after

events.text: Painting included in a public exhibition arranged by Hay.

evidence.quote: until he arranged for it to be included in a public exhibition in 1841

events.text: Bought by the National Gallery, London, as inventory number 186.

evidence.quote: The painting was bought by the National Gallery in London in 1842
It was bought the following year ( 1842 ) by the recently formed National Gallery

undated_mentions: Philip the Good commissioned Jan van Eyck to portray Arnolfini (tapestry order; undated)
Don Diego de Guevara came to own the portrait (before 1516; no exact date)
